title: Cannon Spike
subtitle: Capcom characters in an arena of fire
summary: Cannon Spike is Psikyo's multidirectional arena shooter, released in arcades in 2000 and on Dreamcast later that year.
body: Cannon Spike is Psikyo's multidirectional arena shooter, released in arcades in 2000 and on Dreamcast later that year. Capcom characters including Cammy, Charlie and Arthur fight through concentrated encounters with a strong emphasis on bosses. The player moves around the arena while shooting and striking nearby opponents, with a second player able to join. The crossover provides recognizable faces, but the immediate problem is spatial: keep the character away from danger while maintaining an effective attack on a moving target.

A Mark command locks onto an opponent, separating the choice of target from the direction of movement. Shooting handles distant enemies, while a close-range attack can push back or damage something that gets too near. Combining buttons produces additional ranged and melee specials. A stronger super attack requires a Special Token, making its use a limited resource. These commands give a short encounter several possible responses, from circling a marked boss to clearing the immediate space with a forceful nearby strike.

The seven-character roster reaches across Capcom's games, with Mega Man and Baby Bonnie Hood among the hidden choices. The international title takes its name from Cammy's familiar attack. Psikyo's arcade experience concentrates that collection of characters into brisk stages and boss fights rather than a long narrative journey. The NAOMI arcade hardware made Dreamcast a natural home for the conversion, whose North American release arrived in November 2000. Its appeal comes from seeing familiar characters translated into another studio's shooting vocabulary.
